sections.h2: Where is Mount Pleasant, SC, and how large is the town?
sections.html:
Mount Pleasant is a town in Charleston County on the east side of Charleston Harbor and the tidal Wando River, facing the city of Charleston across the water. Its limits are unusually long: they run about 24 miles northeast along U.S. Route 17, almost to Awendaw.

That shape means a Mount Pleasant address can be a historic street near the harbor, a suburban subdivision, or a lot far up the highway. Each one has a different flood exposure, school zone and commute, and buyers price them differently.

sections.h2: What parts of Mount Pleasant's history still affect its houses?
sections.html:
Settlement here dates to 1680, and the town took the name Mount Pleasant in 1803. Some of that age is still standing: the Hibben House, built in 1755, is described as the town's oldest home.

Three areas show the range of housing stock:

  • The Old Village, the oldest neighborhood, centered on the Pitt Street Shops. The Mount Pleasant Historic District is on the National Register of Historic Places.
  • Scanlonville, one of the first African American communities formed after the Civil War, now annexed into the town.
  • Riverside, which opened in 1930 and is now a gated community.

If you own an older home near the Old Village, ask the Town of Mount Pleasant's planning staff whether exterior repairs need review before you spend money.

sections.h2: How does flood and storm risk change a Mount Pleasant home sale?
sections.html:
Flood risk is the first thing many Mount Pleasant buyers and their lenders check, because the town sits low and borders tidal water. Hurricane Hugo came ashore at Sullivan's Island in September 1989 with an eight-foot surge at Charleston, and one death in Mount Pleasant came from the rising Cooper River, according to the Hugo summary.

Charleston County's flood flyer lists the practical points that show up at closing:

  • A standard homeowners policy generally does not cover flood damage, so flood coverage is a separate policy through the National Flood Insurance Program or a private carrier.
  • A home in a Special Flood Hazard Area with a federally backed mortgage must carry flood insurance.
  • Flood policies typically take effect 30 days after purchase.
  • An insurance agent may ask for an elevation certificate, which a surveyor, engineer or architect can prepare if the town has none on file.

The county flyer gives its own building office number for unincorporated areas and some towns, and says other towns have separate numbers. Call the Town of Mount Pleasant to ask which flood zone a parcel is in and whether an elevation certificate is already on file. A seller who has that paper in hand removes a delay.

sections.h2: Which schools, bridges and roads matter to Mount Pleasant buyers?
sections.html:
Public schools in Mount Pleasant belong to the Charleston County School District, and buyers often ask about the school zone first. The town entry lists these among its public schools and transport links:

  • Wando High School, which opened in 1973, plus Lucy Garrett Beckham High School and Oceanside Collegiate Academy.
  • Middle schools named Laing, Moultrie and Thomas Cario.
  • The Arthur Ravenel Jr. Bridge, an eight-lane cable-stayed span that opened July 16, 2005 and carries U.S. 17 across the Cooper River to Charleston.
  • Charleston International Airport, about 12 miles northwest, and Mount Pleasant Regional Airport (Faison Field) inside the town limits.

School zones are set by the district, so check the district's address lookup rather than relying on a listing description.

sections.h2: How is a Mount Pleasant deed recorded, and what does recording cost?
sections.html:
A deed for a Mount Pleasant house is recorded with the Charleston County Register of Deeds at 101 Meeting Street, Suite 200, in Charleston. The office is open Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and does not take walk-in documents for recording after 4:30 p.m. The phone number is (843) 958-4800. The office says it cannot help you fill out forms.

South Carolina charges a deed recording fee of $1.85 for each $500 of value or fraction of $500. That is $1.30 for the state and $0.55 for the county, under the state code. As an illustration, a $500,000 sale works out to $1,850. The county's own flat recording charges are listed in a fee schedule on its site.

Some transfers are exempt, including deeds of distribution from a decedent's estate and quitclaim or corrective deeds that confirm title the grantee already holds with no payment. An affidavit stating either the value or the reason for the exemption goes with the deed.

sections.h2: When are Mount Pleasant property taxes due, and what happens when you sell?
sections.html:
Charleston County bills Mount Pleasant property taxes, and state law makes them payable between September 30 and January 15. If they are unpaid after January 15, a 3 percent penalty applies, with another 7 percent added if still unpaid before February 2 and another 5 percent before March 17.

The county FAQ says a primary residence is assessed at 4 percent of market value and other real estate at 6 percent. A buyer who will not live in the house, or a seller who has moved out, should expect the higher ratio to matter for who pays what at closing.

The most recent countywide reassessment notices went out in August 2025, and the appeal deadline was November 18, 2025, according to a notice posted by a neighboring town. Most properties are protected by a 15 percent cap on taxable value increases, but sold or transferred property is an exception, so a buyer's bill can differ from the seller's.

Contacts at the county Auditor: real estate at (843) 958-4234 and homestead exemption questions at (843) 958-4200, option 4. A new owner files their own legal residence application. Filing early in the year, before bills are mailed, is the county's own advice.

sections.h2: What must a Mount Pleasant seller disclose?
sections.html:
An owner who sells a house in South Carolina generally gives the buyer a written property condition disclosure on the form set by the Real Estate Commission. The owner may state what they know about each listed condition or state that they make no representation about it.

A knowing false or misleading disclosure can make the owner liable for actual damages, court costs and possibly attorney fees. The statute also leaves room for as-is sales: nothing in it prevents parties from agreeing on the property's condition. Some transfers are exempt, including those by a fiduciary administering an estate, a foreclosure, and a transfer where both sides agree in writing to skip the statement.

The details are in Title 27, Chapter 50. For a specific situation, ask a South Carolina real estate attorney.

sections.h2: What do Mount Pleasant sellers usually run into, and when is a cash sale a fit?
sections.html:
A cash sale can make sense when time, condition or paperwork would slow a traditional listing. These are situations where owners here often consider it:

  • Storm, roof or water damage that would cost money to repair before listing.
  • An inherited house in the town, where heirs live elsewhere and want to avoid carrying it.
  • A flood-zone house where insurance or an elevation certificate is holding up a financed buyer.
  • A rental that the owner no longer wants to manage.

Cash Home Buyers reviews Mount Pleasant houses as they are and explains the numbers in writing. Whether we make an offer depends on the property, and you can compare it with a listing before deciding.

faqs.q: Is Mount Pleasant in Charleston County?
faqs.a: Yes. Mount Pleasant is a town in Charleston County, on the east side of Charleston Harbor. Property tax bills, deed recording and assessments for a house there go through Charleston County offices.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a house in Mount Pleasant?
faqs.a: Deeds are recorded at the Charleston County Register of Deeds, 101 Meeting Street, Suite 200, Charleston. Call (843) 958-4800 to confirm hours and current requirements before you go.

faqs.q: How much is the deed recording fee in South Carolina?
faqs.a: The state code sets the fee at $1.85 per $500 of value, split into $1.30 for the state and $0.55 for the county. Estate distribution deeds and some no-payment transfers are exempt.

faqs.q: Do I need flood insurance to sell a Mount Pleasant house?
faqs.a: The seller does not buy a policy to sell, but a buyer with a federally backed mortgage on a house in a Special Flood Hazard Area must carry flood insurance. Flood policies usually take 30 days to start, so a financed buyer should ask early.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Mount Pleasant house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. South Carolina's disclosure law does not stop an as-is agreement, though you still may owe the buyer the disclosure statement unless your transfer is exempt.

faqs.q: Who do I call about property taxes on my Mount Pleasant house?
faqs.a: Call the Charleston County Auditor at (843) 958-4234 for real estate bills, or (843) 958-4200, option 4, for the homestead exemption.
